content.thinking:
I'm setting up helper imports and a small sphere geometry utility function to streamline building the file's sections.

Still writing geometry helpers...

I'm defining shorthand functions for creating flat-shaded parts and sticks, plus a geometry-merging utility for things like rivets, and starting to sketch the skeleton with a hip joint.

Building the spine chain now, questioning whether assigning "spine" role to both the hips joint and the chain creates a conflict, then deciding to drop the role from the hips joint since it's already the root. I'm continuing into the arm joint setup, iterating over left and right sides.

Writing sleeve bands and cuff details...

Placing finger root points along the palm's elongated sphere, offsetting each finger laterally by its z-coordinate from palm center plus a forward offset along the arm's tangent direction.

I'm computing each finger's three joints by extending from the base point along the palm's forward direction, then curling inward for the middle and tip joints by blending the forward vector with an inward lateral vector, and naming each joint chain by finger (thumb, index, middle, ring, pinky) and side.

I'm sweeping each finger chain with a thin skin-colored tube, flat at the base and rounded at the fingertip, keeping things cartoonish and simple without knuckle bands or nails. Now I'm moving on to building the legs, starting from hip and ankle anchor points scaled by the character's size and feeding them into the limb-building function.

For the legs, I'm thinking through trouser styling options—maybe pinstripes or horizontal stripes to give a whimsical gnome-sock look, with brown trousers possibly featuring knee patches, while boots would cover the lower shaft.

Settling on olive stripes using mustard-brown tones for the trousers, then moving to figure out the foot and boot shaft positioning along the ankle joint.

Now I'm working out the foot sweep path with rounded caps at both ends, extending into a toe region, and placing a toe cap sphere near the toe joint to cap off the boot shape.

Still defining sole outline points...

Now I'm shaping the boot shaft as a rod with flat caps and a gradient darkening toward the bottom, plus adding a separate cuff rod in a brown tone above it.

Next I'm adding buckle straps around the boot with a brass ring loop and darker leather, then moving on to lay out the backpack's extruded outline using relative coordinates for its front profile, centered behind the torso.

I'm applying a leather grain texture to the pack with darker accent stripes, then placing back-facing pocket details using offset z-coordinates on the rear panel.

Now I'm positioning a lower back pocket with beveled top corners, considering a teal canvas patch for contrast against the leather, plus a flap with a brass button. I'm also starting to set up the lid's hinge joint and its horizontal top plate geometry.

Still working out drop plate geometry...

Still placing hardware details...

Simplifying the pipe to a straight run across the bottom with clamps and a small valve wheel instead of the fussy winding path, then sketching the bedroll as a rod with cream cap discs and spiral rings.

I'm adding leather straps with brass buckles wrapped around the bedroll, checking it doesn't clash with the floor or skirt geometry, and placing the wrench on the right side near x -.255.

Now I'm designing the left pouch with a flap holding screwdrivers and a pencil sticking out, then building the telescope on the left shoulder as a series of leather-wrapped cylindrical sections with brass end rings, computing each segment's position along a unit direction vector.

I'm adding the brass sections, an eyepiece lens glowing at the tip, connecting rings at joints, and two leather straps attaching it to the pack. Then I'm starting on the right-side antenna, placing its base and mast endpoint relative to the pack's top lid.

Now I'm working on a propeller mounted at the back of the head, positioning the hub and three blades, but checking the blade radius so the tips don't collide with the head's geometry -- I need to shorten the blade length slightly and offset the starting angle to clear the collision.

Checking the mast height against the hat tip's droop confirms there's no clash between them. Now I'm setting up a lantern accessory with a hook and body positioned on the left side near the bottom of the pack.

Repositioning the pouch and lantern so the chain hangs correctly between them, then mirroring the setup with a copper kettle hooked on the right side, complete with a lathe-turned body, spout, and handle.

Now I'm planning the gauge face with a brass housing ring and a decal texture facing outward, then working out the gear mechanism -- a larger extruded gear with ten teeth meshing against a smaller seven-tooth gear, positioning them so the center distance matches their combined radii along the pack's edge.

I'm also considering extra decorative touches like sticker decal planes on the pack sides and a small lathe-turned horn funnel mounted toward the back of the lid.

For accessories, I'm sketching dangling items like a key ring and small clock on the belt, plus tool pouches with a leather flap, and working out placement for a hammer with cylinder handle and box head hanging at the left hip.

Now I'm adding a few more cute details — a pencil tucked behind the ear with a red/yellow cylinder, and figuring out how to apply a decal patch onto the hat using a projection direction and surface point.

Next I'm designing goggles perched on the hat's front: brass lens rings with glowing cyan glass, a connecting bridge, and a strap loop, positioning them using the hat's nearest-surface point and outward normal for orientation.

Then I move on to the hat band, using a strap loop swept at small radius in dark leather, and consider the hat's surface for ray-hit detection. For the beard, I'm sweeping a catmull curve with a faceted hexagonal cross-section in a beard-colored material, planning to add card details afterward.

Actually, I'm reconsidering scattering tuft cards on the beard surface — might skip that for a simpler low-poly look instead, going with extruded teardrop-shaped locks hanging from the beard front, each defined by a small pointed outline and tilted for a whimsical charm.

Placing five locks along the beard front with staggered x and y positions, extruded outward with a slight thickness, oriented to face forward-down naturally. I'm also sketching two sideburn sweeps curving from ear level down to the chin sides with tapering radius, matching the beard material, then thinking about adding a gradient tint to the lock color for depth.

I'm also considering whether to add age wrinkles, and planning simple SVG assets: a circular gauge texture with colored zones and tick marks, and a small rounded patch icon with a dashed cream stroke and a star or gear shape inside.

Adding badge and swirl icons...

Still writing gear outline logic...

I'm sketching the key bow as a polar clover shape, then adding a glow cylinder for the telescope lens tip, and reconsidering whether the hat's cone joints need a role assignment at all.

Now I'm setting up the hat chain with four named spans along a catmull-rom path, deciding to keep a mottled red paint scheme rather than add decal textures, and working out finger z-offsets for the hand so the palm faces sideways correctly.

Writing thumb and finger geometry...
